title: Starter kits and failure-mode playbook — draft
content:
Purpose
This doc is a working draft for two lightweight artifacts we want to ship together: (A) a small, opinionated "starter kit" for first-time SDK users that runs in <5 minutes, and (B) a failure-mode playbook for engineers and docs writers to surface the most common friction points and how to resolve them. The aim: reduce first-contact support signals and make troubleshooting reproducible for SRE/SEs.

Audience
- New SDK users (engineers) who want to evaluate Redwood API quickly
- Solutions/SEs and support engineers who need step-by-step repros
- Docs writers who will author the final quickstart and troubleshooting pages

Constraints / goals
- Starter kit: runnable locally with minimal deps (curl + python optional), 3 example flows (basic text generation, streaming snippet, simple embedding). Total wall time <= 5 minutes.
- Playbook: short, copyable commands and diagnostic checks prioritized by frequency/impact.
- Prefer copy/paste-first commands; follow-ups with brief explanation.
- Avoid proprietary tokens in public examples; show env-var pattern.

Structure (proposed deliverables)
1) starter-kit/README.md (short, single-file quickstart for SDK)
2) starter-kit/run-local.sh (bash script that runs the three flows)
3) starter-kit/mini-lab.md (3 small exercises for users to tweak prompts)
4) troubleshooting/playbook.md (ranked list of failure modes + commands)
5) docs snippets for website: error-message cookbook, idiomatic recovery examples

Starter kit content (sketch)
- Preflight checklist (1-liners):
  - export REDWOOD_API_KEY=your_key_here
  - python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate || echo "optional: use system python"
  - pip install --upgrade redwood-sdk (if we publish) or point to git install line
- Flow A: simple generation (curl + python example)
  - curl: single POST to /v1/generate with small prompt, print tokens and latency headers
  - python: small snippet using SDK client.generate(prompt=...) printing the text and timing
- Flow B: streaming example
  - CLI: curl -N to /v1/stream and show how to read chunked responses
  - local snippet: use SDK stream iterator, show graceful cancellation (Ctrl-C) and finalization
- Flow C: simple embedding + similarity check
  - create two strings, get embeddings, compute cosine similarity, show thresholding example

Example curl snippet for docs (copy/paste):
  # minimal text-generation
  curl -sS -X POST \\n    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \\n    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n    https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \\n    -d '{"model":"redwood-1-small","input":"Two-sentence summary of Redwood Inference."}' \\
    | jq -r '.output_text'

Notes-to-self: make sure the public endpoint is replaced with regionized example in final docs.

Failure-mode playbook (ranked)
1) Auth errors (401 / 403) — frequency: very high\  Quick checks:
   - echo $REDWOOD_API_KEY | sed -n '1p' || echo "no key"
   - curl -I -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.example/v1/health
   - If 401: check token copy/paste, spaces, shell expansion, KMS rotation windows.
   - If 403: check org/tenant binding, route-level permissions (Dedicated/Private tokens differ).
2) Slow initial tokens / cold start spikes — frequency: high\  Quick checks:
   - Reproduce with consistent prompt, measure p50/p95 latency for first N requests
   - Check headers: X-Redwood-Serve-TTI (or equivalent) for kernel warm time (internal header name TBD)
   - Workarounds: recommend short warmup burst, use pinned dedicated capacity, or model variant with smaller context window.
3) Streaming truncated or missing chunks — freq: medium\  Quick checks:
   - Use curl -v -N to see chunk boundaries, confirm Content-Type: text/event-stream or chunked encoding
   - Verify client read loop does not time out; increase socket read timeouts in SDK/requests for long streams
4) Unexpected output format / JSON parse failures — freq: medium\  Quick checks:
   - Surround generation call with a stricter schema or content filter in code; dump raw output to logs before parsing
   - If model returns extra whitespace/newlines, apply a safe rstrip() and then JSON parse
5) Embedding regressions / drift — freq: low->medium\  Quick checks:
   - Recompute embeddings on canonical probe-set, compare cosine similarity baseline in CI
   - If drift detected after model swap, enable auto-fallback to previous embedding model in routing policy
6) Quota/Rate-limit errors (429) — freq: medium\  Quick checks:
   - Parse Retry-After header; implement exponential backoff with jitter; batch small requests where appropriate
7) Misleading latency diagnostics — freq: low\  Quick checks:
   - Confirm whether latency is client-side (DNS, TLS handshake) vs server-side (per-token time). Use curl -w '%{time_starttransfer}\\n' to capture TTFB.

Repro scripts / one-liners (copy/paste)
- Check auth header and minimal generate:
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{time_total}\\n' -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -d '{"model":"redwood-1-small","input":"ping"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate

- Stream diagnostic (shows chunk timing):
  { time curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream -d '{"model":"redwood-1-small","input":"stream test"}'; } 2>&1 | ts

- Local embedding check (python snippet):
  python - <<'PY'
  import os,sys,time,math
  from requests import post
  key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY')
  r=post('https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings', headers={'Authorization':f'Bearer {key}','Content-Type':'application/json'}, json={'model':'embed-small','input':['a','b']})
  print(r.status_code, r.text[:400])
  PY

Developer UX: error messages and doc signals
- Draft guidance for SDK error strings: always include HTTP code, short reason, unique error id (for search in logs), and a suggested next-action. Example: "redwood.auth.invalid_key (401): API key invalid — check REDWOOD_API_KEY env var and ensure no leading/trailing quotes. If using a rotated key, wait 30s and retry. See DX-914."
- For streaming cancellation, show 'graceful_cancel()' example in both JS and Python. Explain partial output semantics.

CI / test automation suggestions (mini-suite)
- Add a lightweight CI job 'sdk-smoke' that runs against sandbox endpoint (not prod) that does:
  - auth check, small generate, small embed, streaming connect/disconnect
  - measure p50, p95 and fail build if generate latency > 3s p50 or any 5xx seen
- Add regression probe for embeddings: canonical 10-sentence probe with stored baseline vector similarities; fail if top-1 similarity drops by >0.05.

Authoring checklist for final docs
- Finalize public endpoint URLs (region examples)
- Replace internal header names with public equivalents or hide them behind "X-Redwood-" prefix
- Get security review for token examples and sandbox account provisioning
- Add inline troubleshooting expanders for each quickstart step (folded by default)
- Add a short video GIF for streaming demo (3–5s)

Outstanding questions / TODOs
- Which sandbox domain should we use for public quickstart vs. internal test? (Marco to confirm)
- Decide on exact header names we expose for kernel warm times and routing metadata (engineering infra input)
- Auth: do we want the quickstart to show both API key and SDK-config-file flows? (Pros/cons)
- Should we include a small 'node' example in the starter kit? (Priya to prototype)

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep starter kit under 150 lines total if possible.
- Make the first section purely hand-holdy: "You have 3 minutes? Follow these 3 commands and you'll see text."
- For playbook, prefer minimal mental model rather than exhaustive list. Think "show first, then explain" approach.

Appendix: minimal flow timeline for UX designers
- Step 0: Sign up, get API key (30s)
- Step 1: paste key and run the 3 commands (2–3 minutes)
- Step 2: read the outputs, try edit prompt (1–2 minutes)
- Expected: most users either continue to embed or reach for example app after 5–8 minutes.

Contact / ownership
- Primary owner: Ivy Chen (eng-developer-experience)
- Draft contributors: Marco Rivera, Priya Patel, Evan Liu

Change log (working)
- 2025-11-03: initial sketch
- 2026-01-08: added CI probes and repro scripts (Marco)
- 2026-02-20: added auth troubleshooting and authoring checklist (Ivy)

End of draft.
